title: Love made visible
hook: Gibran: work is love made visible (The Prophet, 1923)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was useful work: William Morris's hopes of rest, product and pleasure. Your line was pleasure in the work itself. Today, a poet who says what good work is made of.

A ship is waiting in the harbor to take a man home after years away. Before he boards, the people of the city gather around him and, one by one, ask him to speak. About love. About marriage. About children. Later a farmer, a ploughman, steps forward and asks him to speak of work. That's a scene from The Prophet, a book by the Lebanese American poet Kahlil Gibran. The man is Almustafa, and inside his long answer about work sit five words: "Work is love made visible." Today's word is the one who said it: Almustafa.
screen: `A SHIP IN THE HARBOR.` → `A FARMER ASKS ABOUT WORK.` → `FIVE WORDS.`

segments.voice: First, the claim itself. Love, on its own, can't be seen; you can't photograph it. But a meal can be seen. A mended coat. A swept step. In Almustafa's answer, work is where love leaves the inside of a person and becomes something you can touch. Second, what working with love looks like, in paraphrase: weaving cloth with threads drawn from your own heart, as if someone you love would wear it. Building a house as if your beloved would live in it. Sowing seeds with tenderness, as if the one you love would eat the harvest. The test is simple: who is this for, in your mind, while you make it? Third, the hard half. Almustafa warns, again in paraphrase, that bread baked with indifference is bitter bread, and feeds only half of a person's hunger. Grudge the crushing of the grapes, he says, and the grudge becomes a poison in the wine. The same loaf, two different breads. Fourth, how this gathers up the days just before it. Ihsan asked for excellence, as though seen. Qing forgot the prize. Ruskin wanted joy in the making. Morris wanted hope in it. Gibran names what might be underneath all of them: the person you're doing it for. It doesn't have to be grand. A shirt ironed for a parent's interview. A gate fixed before a neighbor gets home. Seen this way, an ordinary chore is a small, visible message, even if nobody ever reads it as one.
screen: `LOVE YOU CAN TOUCH.` · `AS IF THE BELOVED WOULD WEAR IT.` · `BITTER BREAD.` · `WHO IS IT FOR?` · then, large: `WORK IS LOVE MADE VISIBLE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone you love, and let their face come clear. Think of one small job you could do for them, folding their laundry, cooking the dish they like, and picture doing it slowly with them in mind the whole time, the way Almustafa describes weaving cloth for the beloved. If you pray, you can hold them in your own tradition's words.
Almustafa. The speaker in Gibran's The Prophet who tells the ploughman that work is love made visible. Today's word.
Your line: a small, visible message. Who is it for? That's day nine hundred six.

howItsDone: Readers of The Prophet, including some people who keep a spiritual life outside any one tradition, return to its chapter on work when they think about their own work.
